persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Sarah, 34, a mother in Illinois, USA. Her son Noah is 8 and goes to the kids' class at their church every Sunday (in America they call it Kids' Church, like Sunday school). Tonight is Wednesday. Noah did a kind thing this week, and you want to read this week's page with him and give him his star.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called The Clubhouse. You have never seen it, and that is fine. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Every Sunday, children at church learn a Bible story and a verse. The teacher gives them a paper to take home.
But the paper gets lost in the car before Monday. By Wednesday, nobody remembers the story or the verse.
Many parents would like a phone app for this. But most apps for children have adverts, chat with strangers, or an account to make. Parents worry, and they are right to worry.
The Clubhouse solves both problems. It is one page from the church to the children. The church writes. The family reads. That is all.
There are no accounts. There is no chat. There are no adverts. Nobody can send a message to your child in this app. Only the church can put words here.
Who uses it? Children, with their parents, at home during the week. The children's leader at church changes the page once a week, in about five minutes.
Now let us walk through the page slowly, from the top.

lines.t: At the top is the name, The Clubhouse, and the name of the church's children's group. Here it is Immanuel Kids.

lines: Below that is a blue card. It is a short hello from the children's leaders, about what is happening this week.

lines.t: The next card is called This week at Kids' Church. It gives the title of this week's lesson, a few words about the story, and what to bring on Sunday.
Next is the yellow card, Verse of the week. A verse is a short piece of the Bible for the children to learn by heart.
Under the verse is a button, Read it to me. Tap it, and the phone reads the verse out loud. This helps small children who cannot read well yet.

lines: Then comes the pink card, Challenge of the week. It is one small thing to do at home this week. This week it is a secret kindness mission: do one kind thing without anyone seeing.

lines.t: When the child has done the challenge, tap the big button, I did it, with the star. The child earns one star, and the button changes to say Done, see you Sunday.

lines: You can earn only one star each week. If you tap the button again, nothing changes. Next week, when the church changes the challenge, there is a new star to earn.
The stars stay only on this phone. Not even the church can see them. They are just for the child.

lines.t: At the bottom are coloured boxes with big numbers. These are countdowns. Each one shows how many days until a fun event at church.

lines: One event is called Trunk or Treat. That is an American church party at the end of October, where children collect sweets from the back of cars. Another is shoeboxes, which are gift boxes for poor children at Christmas.
When an event day has passed, its box goes away by itself.
To start again, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh, erase this app's data. The app asks you twice before it erases the stars.
In the test, you will be a parent with a child at this church. Read the page the way a family would. If anything is confusing, say so. Confusing parts are exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Sarah, sitting with Noah on Wednesday night. The star has not been given yet. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Some questions you answer in your own words. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open The Clubhouse. If the welcome card shows, tap 'skip the tour' → 'Let’s go ›'. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. (If it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', tap OK: the app is already empty.) The challenge button now says 'I did it! ⭐' with no stars under it. (Verified 10 Oct: the star check is false after this.)
challenge.challengeNote: The Clubhouse saves only one thing on the phone: this week's star. Everything else on the page is written by the church, so tasks 2 to 5 are questions the student answers by reading the page (check = null, selfReport). Only task 1 is checked automatically.

tasks.text: Noah did his secret kind thing this week: he set the table without being asked. Give him this week's star.
tasks.hint: Look at the Challenge of the week card. There is one big button there for when the challenge is done.

tasks.text: Noah wants to learn this week's verse. What does the verse begin with, and where in the Bible is it from?
tasks.selfReport: Write the first words of the verse and where it is from.
tasks.answer: “Be strong and courageous…” from Joshua 1:9 (the Verse of the week card).
tasks.hint: Find the yellow card called Verse of the week.

tasks.text: What must Noah bring to church this Sunday?
tasks.answer: His Bible (if he has one) and his best joke for Joke Minute (the This week at Kids' Church card).
tasks.hint: Read the This week at Kids' Church card to the end.

tasks.text: Noah asks: how many days until the Christmas pageant (the church Christmas play)? Find the answer in the app. Do not count on a calendar.
tasks.selfReport: Write the number of days the app shows.
tasks.answer: The big number in the Christmas pageant box at the bottom (71 on 10 Oct 2026; it goes down by one each day).
tasks.hint: Look at the coloured boxes with big numbers under the challenge card.

tasks.text: Another parent asks you: 'Can a stranger send my child a message in this app?' What do you tell her, and why?
tasks.selfReport: Write your answer to the other parent.
tasks.answer: No. There is no chat, no account and no adverts; only the church can put words on the page.
tasks.hint: Think about what the app has and does not have. The words at the very bottom of the page help.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a weekly page from the church for children and parents (lesson, verse, challenge)
safe: no chat, no adverts, no accounts, nothing from strangers
a star for doing the challenge, and countdowns to church events
